shape.text: A legacy private app generates an access token unique to that app, sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header; changes to the app's scopes update what the token can do but not the token string.
HubSpot's token information request takes the private app access token in a tokenKey body field and returns the creating user, the Hub ID, the private app ID and the scopes.
No prefix, region marker, alphabet, length or grouping of a private app access token is established.

unresolved.reason: The pages read state none; their only token strings in this area are masked or placeholder values. Third-party pattern lists show a pat-na1-/pat-eu1- layout from one maintainer and a UUID-shaped layout of unspecified target from two. A HubSpot statement or two independent maintainers' artifacts that target private app tokens would settle it.

issuance.text: A legacy private app is created in a HubSpot account under Development, Legacy apps, by a super admin, and its token is revealed on the app's Auth tab.

HubSpot has announced that creating new legacy private apps through the account UI is being disabled on 2026-09-28 for new accounts and 2026-10-26 for older accounts, while existing legacy private apps continue to work.

lifecycle.text: A private app token can be rotated, which creates a new token and expires the original immediately or after about 7 days; HubSpot recommends rotating every six months, and deleting the app revokes the token permanently.

collisions.text: HubSpot says private app access tokens are implemented on top of OAuth, without stating that their string format is the same as an OAuth access token's.
Whether the legacy private app token and the static auth access token of project-based apps are one credential family is not established.

unresolved.reason: Neither page read mentions the other credential or states that the strings share a format or lifecycle. A HubSpot statement relating them would settle it.

openQuestions.text: Whether the tokens of the replacement Service Keys or project-based apps share the legacy private app token layout is not established.

unresolved.reason: The changelog names Service Keys as the replacement but no page read states any token layout. A HubSpot statement for each credential would settle it.

notes: Project-authored by the maintainers of this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
